characterization_methods.key_findings: 2Al composition shows the minimum UTS/TE trend and lowest-strength cluster (see properties).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: mechanical screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness nearly flat at ~200 HBW from 0Al to 6Al.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: rolling plane; samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in final materials; as-cast coarse dendritic microstructure; hot rolling + water quenching gives fully recrystallized ~20 µm grains with retained Mn microsegregations.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction by grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques

characterization_methods.purpose: specimen preparation for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation

interfaces.interface_notes: Single-phase austenite; no phase interfaces reported. j-carbide/matrix interface details in the paper (lattice mismatch below 3% with austenitic matrix) are not specifically reported for this 2 wt.% Al sample.
interfaces.slip_behavior: TWIP effect prevails as the deformation mechanism: dislocation-based strain hardening followed at higher loads by mechanical twinning

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al properties fall between those of Fe-30Mn-1.2C (no Al) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al; aging has a much smaller influence on tensile behavior for the 2–6 wt.% Al intermediate variants than for the 8 wt.% Al variant.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace, successively filled from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: 10 × 50 × 130 mm³ blocks → 2 ± 0.1 mm thick, ~500 mm long sheets

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: After reheating/water quenching, sheets were cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments (2 × 60 × 55 mm³) per alloy composition.
Followed by water quenching; this is the parent process (proc_homog-1100c-2h-wq) referenced for the aged sample.
Aging conducted in air at 450, 500, 550, and 600 °C for 0 h, 1 h, and 24 h each, followed by oil quenching; this specific sample corresponds to the 600 °C / 1 h condition.

Scales removed from surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments; samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation prepared from segments by package spark erosion.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: prepared from 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ segments by package spark erosion

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase recrystallized austenite (fcc) with TWIP/SIMPLEX deformation behavior; Al content below 5 wt.% favors a single austenite phase at room temperature.

unmapped_findings: General literature range for austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys (not specific to this 600 °C/1 h sample): yield strength 0.5–1.0 GPa, elongation to fracture 30–80%, ultimate tensile strength 1.0–1.5 GPa (block b0014).

κ-carbide (L′1₂, non-oxide perovskite) general crystallographic facts from the paper: ordered fcc structure, approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)₃AlC, lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to an austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix enabling cuboidal nanoprecipitates; formation in this 2 wt.% Al sample is not clearly reported (block b0015).

The paper attributes pronounced aging-induced strengthening and nm-sized κ-carbide formation mainly to the high-Al (~8 wt.%) variant; the 2–6 wt.% Al intermediate variants (including 2Al) show a much smaller influence of aging on tensile behavior (blocks b0025).

κ-carbides are described as thermally very stable at 600 °C, prevailing after 100 h heat treatment with only modest coarsening; the supporting Fig. 5 data are for Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al after 24 h at 600 °C, not for the 2Al sample (blocks b0025, b0034).

A temperature-sensitive constitutive strain-hardening model (Steinmetz et al.) for fcc low-SFE TWIP/SIMPLEX steels is described, but its validation data are for a Fe-22Mn-0.6C model TWIP steel, not for this Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al sample (blocks b0036–b0100, figure_007).
